name: queries/apps.py
summary: Django AppConfig class that registers and configures the queries application within the project.
purpose: Exists to inform Django's application registry about the queries app, enabling discovery, metadata attachment, and lifecycle management so the framework can correctly load models, URLs, and other app-level resources.
responsibilities: Register the queries app in Django's global app registry
Provide application metadata such as name, label, and default configuration
Act as a dedicated hook for application initialization logic (e.g., signals, checks, or app-specific setup)
Decouple app-level configuration from models, views, and business logic
inputs: Project INSTALLED_APPS setting entry pointing to this configuration
outputs: Application metadata consumed by Django's app loading system
architecture_notes: Follows Django's standard AppConfig pattern to encapsulate per-application metadata and lifecycle hooks. Isolates the queries app as a self-contained deployable unit within the backend/apps directory, keeping startup logic out of models.py and preventing circular import issues.
improvements: Add explicit 'name' and 'verbose_name' class attributes for readability
Implement the ready() method if signal registration or startup initialization is needed
Add type hints and module-level docstrings to improve maintainability
Define 'default_auto_field' if the app contains models to suppress Django system checks
